notes: single quotes prevent substitution - nothing is fetched or executed

CORRECTED 2026-10-08: labelled negative in error. Single quotes stop the OUTER shell only; `sh -c` / `bash -c` then execute the string AS SHELL, which performs the substitution and runs the fetched code. Verified empirically: bash -c '$(echo echo X)' prints X. Independent review (Codex) had this right.
